name: SWERVE
source: Sandia Winged Energetic Re-entry Vehicle (SWERVE). Three flights 1979-1985 from the Kauai Test Facility on STRYPI boosters; flight 3 reentered near Johnston Island (~1,180 km). Spherically blunted 5.25-deg half-angle cone, 'a little over 100 in' long (~2.6 m), with small wings/elevons for lift and control, Mach 2-14 maneuvering. Nose-tip/heat-shield ablative. (Primary: Sandia hypersonics descriptions; the AHW conical glide body is described as 'SWERVE with improved TPS'.)
notes: GEOMETRY is sourced: 5.25-deg sphere-cone, nose_radius from the published R_n/R_base = 0.07 (R_base = L*tan(5.25) ~ 0.238 m -> R_n ~ 0.0167 m, sharper than the AHW model's 0.05 placeholder). base diameter 0.476 m is the CONE base; the ~0.61 m (2 ft) factsheet 'diameter' includes the wings. MASS ~400 kg is ESTIMATED from beta = m/(Cd*A): beta = 15,250 kg/m2 (published flight-vehicle value, same-size 2.75 m SWERVE-derived Mars vehicle) x Cd*A (cone base area 0.178 m2, Cd ~0.10-0.20) -> 270-540 kg, central ~400. CALIBRATED to ~350 kg by flying Strypi VIII R to the known ~1,180 km Kauai->Johnston range (350 kg -> ~1,130 km, 300 kg -> ~1,250 km on a flat loft; implies Cd ~0.12). Mass is coupled to the assumed loft shape, so treat as ~300-400 kg. L/D 1.5 is a representative winged-cone value (same airframe as the AHW model, per the SWERVE->AHW heritage). tps_material = carbon_ablator (the ORIGINAL ablative heat shield); the SWERVE->AHW claim is that the airframe was reused with an improved heat shield for the longer AHW range, so the AHW RV should differ from this mainly in TPS, not airframe.
